questions.question_text:
The diagram shows a right-angled triangle with unknown side $x$, a side of $10\text{cm}$, and hypotenuse $20\text{cm}$.
Which is the correct method to work out the unknown side?

options.why: This finds the square of the unknown side, not the side itself.
The hypotenuse should be subtracted when finding a shorter side.
Adding produces a value larger than the hypotenuse.

questions.solution_text: Using Pythagoras, $x^2 + 10^2 = 20^2$. Rearranging and taking the square root gives $x = \sqrt{20^2 - 10^2}$.
